summary: Alert Slack links resolve to 404 after saved query parameter rename
description: Issue summary: Several Slack alert notifications from Acme AI contain 'Open dashboard' / 'View query' links that return 404 or resolve to a different org context after the customer renamed a saved query parameter earlier this week. Impact: Customers cannot follow alert links to investigate, increasing time-to-resolution and triggering support escalations. Affects alerts created before the parameter rename and some alerts evaluated after retention compaction windows. Observed for multiple teams at Acme AI; roughly 20% of alerts for a single org failed in a sample sweep.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create saved query with a templated variable named 'env'. 2) Create an alert based on that saved query that posts to Slack. 3) Rename variable 'env' -> 'environment' in saved query settings. 4) Wait for next evaluation or trigger manual re-eval of alert. 5) Click the 'View query' or 'Open dashboard' link in Slack notification. Expected: link opens query in Console with param prefilled. Actual: 404 or opens a query page with missing variable context causing UI redirect to org root.
logs: Alert eval log snippet (2026-03-09T14:22:11Z): eval_id=ae-88c3, query_uuid=8f2b3a, saved_query_slug=team-health, param_snapshot_id=ps-447, link_url=/orgs/1234/console/dashboards/team-health?var-env=prod -> 404. Retention compaction job log (2026-03-07T03:00:00Z): compaction-run-id=comp-20260307-01, pruned-metadata=param-name-mapping: dropped-old-name 'env' -> 'environment' mapping missing.
investigation_notes: Timeline: Customer renamed variable on 2026-03-06. A retention compaction job ran 2026-03-07 that pruned stale parameter name mappings. Alerts evaluated on 2026-03-09 started generating Slack links that reference the old variable name. Hypothesis: Alert link generation concatenates saved_query_slug + last_known_variable_name (non-stable) rather than using saved_query UUID or a stable link generator. When compaction prunes the variable-name mapping, link generation falls back to the stale key and results in a broken route. Reproduced locally by simulating compaction and renaming flow. Root cause appears to be in console/alert-link-generator service (code path: console/links/alert_links.py) where we compute link querystring using variable names from a soft-metadata table instead of canonical variable UUID. Also observed race when alerts are re-evaluated during metadata backfill which results in mixed old/new links.
comments: Support (2026-03-09) - Kathryn Rivera: Initial triage with customer. Confirmed 13/60 alerts in sample have 404 links. Customer provided Slack message examples and one workspace notification timestamped 2026-03-09T14:24:10Z.

SRE (2026-03-10) - Omar Patel: Reproduced in staging using compaction job artifact. Alerts posted with outdated 'var-ENV' keys producing 404. Captured eval trace ae-88c3 and confirmed missing mapping in param_snapshot table.

ENG (2026-03-11) - Diego Morales: Identified bad code path in alert_links.py where link builder uses param_display_name instead of param_uuid. Preparing patch to use stable UUID and fall back to mapping table if UUID missing.

Support (2026-03-12) - Alyssa Chen: Communicated interim mitigation to customer: recommended re-saving affected alerts and performing a manual re-eval. Customer requested ETA for permanent fix and a backfill for historical alerts.

ENG (2026-03-12) - Diego Morales: Deployed hotfix to staging (console hotfix v1.8.3-hotfix) that changes link generation to prefer saved_query_uuid and param_uuid. Running a subset deployment to prod as canary now.
resolution: Workaround: Instructed customer to resave the saved query (which regenerates stable param UUIDs) or to edit the alert and save to rehydrate links. Hotfix: Deployed change to alert link generator to construct links using stable saved_query_uuid and param_uuid. Backfill: A migration job 'alert-link-backfill-933210' scheduled to run 2026-03-13 will scan alerts created before 2026-03-07 and rewrite link metadata to point to canonical UUIDs. Monitoring: Post-deploy checks include sampling 1000 alerts across orgs for 404 rate drop and Slack link resolution success. Follow-ups: 1) Add unit and integration tests to prevent regressions; 2) Add a console runbook step to run backfill after retention compaction; 3) Improve telemetry to surface link-generation errors in real-time (new metric: alert.link_generation.failures).
next_steps: 1) Complete prod canary rollout for hotfix and validate 404 rate in sampling dashboard (ENG). 2) Run alert-link-backfill-933210 during low-traffic window and verify results with customer (SRE/Support). 3) Add regression test to CI that simulates parameter rename + compaction (ENG). 4) Create a short Confluence doc describing the safe rename process for saved query variables (Support/Docs).
